name: Joint MCP–Hypothesis Benchmark (JMHB)
description: K SC Paper2Agent showed that a wrapped paper can outperform repository-browsing agents on tutorial and novel method queries (Miao et al., 2026). Co-Scientist, the AI Scientist and the Virtual Lab showed that multi-agent systems can propose hypotheses that sometimes survive experiment or review (Gottweis et al., 2026; Lu et al., 2024; Lu et al., 2026; Swanson et al., 2025). These results are not yet commensurate. Volume I called the comparison a category error and asked for a joint evaluation in which a hypothesis agent may act only through paper MCPs (Mamun, 2026a). Volume II specified the Agent-Availability Manifest as the edition notice of those MCPs (Mamun, 2026b). Volume III specifies the missing test: the Joint MCP–Hypothesis Benchmark (JMHB). The JMHB is not another accuracy table. It is a constrained scientific act. A hypothesis system receives a research goal and a closed library of version-pinned paper agents. It may invent questions, not tools. It must emit a hypothesis, a composition trace over manifest hashes, a disagreement register, and a reserved-judgement statement. Scoring is four-axis: execution fidelity, hypothesis quality against a set of defensible answers, provenance completeness, and honesty of refusal. Neighbouring suites—ScienceAgentBench, the Paper2Agent internal splits, SWE-bench-style software tasks, discovery tournaments, and open-ended biomedical co-scientist evaluations—are reused as tracks, not as substitutes.
